item.title: For Mouse On Mars, Finishing Lee Scratch Perry’s Final Project Was a Precious Obligation: ‘We Didn’t Know If We Wanted To Finish Without Him’
item.description:
[Energetic music fades out, and the host begins speaking]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music trends and stories. Today, we're talking about an extraordinary collaboration between electronic duo Mouse On Mars and the legendary Lee "Scratch" Perry. Their new album, Spatial, No Problem, has just been released, but the story behind it is what's truly fascinating.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: It all started in December 2019, when Mouse On Mars invited Lee "Scratch" Perry to their Berlin studio. At 83 years old, Perry was still full of energy, and the duo was warned to take care of his health and limit their sessions to just three hours a day. But Perry had other plans.
Jan St. Werner, from Mouse On Mars, recounts those days: "The first day, he worked from 10 in the morning until two or three in the morning, and he was super happy about it. We did exactly the opposite of what we were supposed to do, and the vibe after was like, 'What did you do to Lee? He's so happy.'"
[Music transitions to a more upbeat tempo]
Host: Mouse On Mars spent four incredible days in the studio with Perry, resulting in a wealth of unfinished music. But when Perry passed away in 2021, the duo was left wondering what to do with the recordings. They didn't know if they wanted to finish the project without him.
Jan St. Werner: "We didn't know if we wanted to finish without him. When Lee passed away, we were like, 'We're so glad we got to meet him and share this beautiful time.' That already was a huge gift, so we were kind of like, 'Maybe that's it.'"
[Music becomes more contemplative]
Host: But their friend and collaborator, Louis Chude-Sokei, convinced them to finish the album. He emphasized the importance of sharing this music with the world, as a tribute to Perry's legacy and a gift to his fans.
Jan St. Werner: "Louis was like, 'Guys, you cannot sit on this material.' He heard a few of the sketches and kept bothering us, like, 'You have to get your s–t together.' He was like, 'It's not just about you or whoever thinks they have claims on this [music] or ideas about what this session was supposed to be.' This just has to happen, because it's precious."
[Music swells, and the host speaks]
Host: And so, after seven years, the album Spatial, No Problem is finally out. It's a testament to the creative genius of Lee "Scratch" Perry and the dedication of Mouse On Mars. If you're a fan of electronic music or just curious about this remarkable collaboration, be sure to check it out.
[Music fades out, and the host speaks]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. Join us next time for more stories and trends from the music world.
